cover.woman_bio: Ophthalmologist. She was the first African American resident in ophthalmology at New York University, proposed the field of community ophthalmology, and in 1983 became the first woman in the United States to chair an ophthalmology residency program.

content.content: Timed practice. Set a timer for 45 minutes: 5 to read and plan, 35 to write, 5 to read aloud and fix. Type your essay. Your first paragraph must contain your main idea sentence that picks a side. Use evidence from BOTH passages (at least one number from each), answer the other side once, and end with a Link. Read each sentence aloud and fix fragments. Do not stop to look up spelling.

Practice passages (invented for this exercise; the numbers are NOT from real studies). Should a city turn some car-parking spaces into bike lanes?

Passage A. After a city replaced 150 parking spaces with protected bike lanes, daily bike trips on that road rose from 2,000 to 5,000 and street injuries fell by 30%. Cleaner air along the road also meant fewer breathing problems reported at the nearby clinic.

Passage B. The same road had 400 parking spaces before the change, and 250 after. Shop owners reported that sales fell 12% in the first year, because customers who drove could no longer find a place to park. Delivery vans also began stopping in the traffic lane, which slowed buses.

content.question: Plan (5 minutes). Which position is better supported? Write your main idea sentence, then list the number you will quote from A, the number you will quote from B, and the other side’s best point with your reply.
Write your essay here (about 35 minutes). Which position is better supported: replacing parking with bike lanes, or keeping the parking? Explain your choice with evidence from both passages.

pomodoros.subject: Social Studies: the Constitution and the vote

content.content: Key amendments: the First Amendment protects freedom of religion, speech, the press, assembly and petition. The 13th (1865) ended slavery. The 14th (1868) guaranteed equal protection of the laws. The 15th (1870) said a citizen cannot be denied the vote because of race. The 19th (1920) gave women the vote. The 26th (1971) lowered the voting age to 18. The President can veto a bill, but Congress can override a veto with a two-thirds vote in both houses.
Multiple-choice rule: tap ONE letter only. If you change your mind, tap the one you want instead.

content.question: Which amendment protects freedom of speech?

choices: A) A simple majority in one house
B) A two-thirds vote in both houses

content.content: Dr. Patricia Bath (1942–2019) trained in eye medicine at New York University from 1970 to 1973, where she was the first African American resident in ophthalmology. She noticed that blindness was twice as common among Black patients as among white patients, and she traced much of the difference to a lack of access to eye care. She proposed a new field called community ophthalmology, which brings eye care to people who are underserved, and in 1977 she and three colleagues founded the American Institute for the Prevention of Blindness. In 1983 she became the first woman in the United States to chair an ophthalmology residency program. She thought of a new laser device for cataract surgery in 1981, and it took her nearly five years to finish the research and apply for a patent. (Practice passage written for this packet from the National Library of Medicine biography of Dr. Patricia E. Bath, nlm.nih.gov.)
Multiple-choice rule: tap ONE letter only. If you change your mind, tap the one you want instead.

content.question: What is the main idea of the passage?

C) New York University is old.

choices: A) She believed good eye care should reach everyone.
B) She did not want to work with patients.

Dr. Bath said: “The ability to restore sight is the ultimate reward.” In 2 or 3 complete sentences: what is a reward in your work that is bigger than a grade?
